payload.public_title: Reported substantial MCAS improvement — secondhand community lead
payload.public_paraphrase: A community member reports that an adult friend with reported mast cell activation syndrome experienced substantial improvement while using a combination of low-dose naltrexone, low-dose NAD+ injections, and low-dose tirzepatide. This is a one-hop report relayed by a friend, has not been independently verified, and currently lacks enough diagnostic, sequencing, timing, dose, co-intervention, adverse-effect, and follow-up detail to attribute the improvement to the combination or any component. AskRigor retains it as a public lead for follow-up, similar-report discovery, evidence checking, and future research design.
payload.source_distance_label: Reported by a friend who says the affected person told them; not a firsthand subject report

redactions_or_generalizations: Omitted the affected person's name and relationship-specific identifying detail.
Used an adult age band rather than exact age.
Omitted location, clinician, clinic, dates, records, and direct quotations.
deidentification_review.rationale: The public version contains only a broad adult subject description, reported condition, three intervention names, and a high-level outcome. It does not expose a direct identifier, direct private quotation, document, media, exact location, or exact date. This is a synthetic fixture and not a real publication.

limitations: The report is secondhand and has not been independently verified.
The MCAS diagnostic basis is unknown.
The doses, formulations, frequencies, start dates, sequence, overlap, adherence, and stopping or restarting are unknown.
Other medications, diet, infections, environment, and life changes are unknown.
The baseline, exact outcomes, time to improvement, durability, current status, and adverse effects are incompletely described.
This lead cannot establish efficacy, causality, population frequency, or which component mattered.
